dial.summary: Six of eight macro indicators remain constructive on August 15 — the 2s10s yield curve steepened to +51bps and DXY fell to 99.63 as soft July retail sales (August 14) reinforced reduced September rate-hike probability; ISM Manufacturing holds at a 4-year high of 55.6%, global M2 continues expanding, Fed balance sheet steady at ~$6.74T, and BTC funding rates near zero; real yields remain the lone structural headwind at ~2.38%; BTC dominance at 56.06% holds well above the 55% Alt Rotation trigger — dial stays at BTC Accumulation heading into the decisive PCE/GDP Q2 second estimate/Jackson Hole cluster (August 26–28), where Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural keynote is the dominant macro catalyst for this cycle.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: US M2 at $23.2T as of June 2026 (H.6 released July 28, 2026; ~5.5% YoY growth, 29th consecutive monthly increase); next H.6 release August 25, 2026 (July data); 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) last confirmed at ~$102.7T in June 2026 via MacroMicro — July 2026 global aggregate not yet published; value carried forward at ~$103.2T on continued expansion trajectory; 4-week trend up (US M2 expansion confirmed through June, YoY growth +5.5% — contracting YoY headwind condition not met); status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed, no YoY contraction in any major central bank aggregate).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3) remains the most recent reading — August data releases September 1, 2026; sub-indexes: Production 58.5%, New Orders 56.7%, Employment 52.8% (first factory employment expansion in 33 months), Prices Paid 71.1%; 4-week trend up: June 53.3% → July 55.6% = +2.3pp, seventh consecutive expansion month, highest reading since May 2022; August 14 soft July retail sales add demand-side caution but do not change the July manufacturing expansion signal; status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds of <48 falling or >62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.63 (August 14, 2026 close, -0.22% on the day); fell on soft July retail sales data ('DXY Falls after Weak Retail Sales Data' — TradingEconomics) as reduced September rate-hike probability weighed on the dollar; 4-week trend down: ~101.4 (mid-July) → 99.63 (August 14) = -1.7%, above the 0.5% flat threshold; status NEUTRAL (ICE DXY in the 97.5–100 neutral band; approaching the 97.5 supportive threshold as dollar weakens on cooling Fed rate-hike expectations ahead of Jackson Hole August 28; trending toward the supportive zone if PCE and/or Warsh tone deliver dovish surprise).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield) estimated at ~2.38% for August 14 — FRED API blocked by network egress proxy; July 23 TIPS auction cleared at 2.438% real yield (TIPs Watch, highest at auction since October 2008); nominal DGS10 eased to 4.68% on August 14 (down from ~4.70% on August 13) after soft July retail sales cut rate-hike expectations, implying marginal real yield compression; 4-week trend up: ~2.18% (early July) → ~2.38% (August 14 estimate) = +20bps, above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (above 2% threshold; real yields structurally elevated — easing toward 2% threshold is the key watch into PCE August 26 and Jackson Hole August 28).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 14 close: DGS10 4.68%, DGS2 4.17%, spread = +51bps; notable steepening on the day as soft July retail sales drove short-end (2Y) yields lower faster than long-end (2Y fell ~7bps vs 10Y ~2bps), consistent with rate-cut repricing at the front end; 4-week trend up: ~35bps (mid-July) → +51bps (August 14) = +16bps steepening, above the 5bps flat threshold; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening; if Warsh signals a dovish September at Jackson Hole August 28, the front end could rally further and steepen the curve toward 70–80bps).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL latest: ~$6.74T for week ending August 13, 2026 per H.4.1 released August 13 (slight decline from $6.75T for week ending August 5); next H.4.1 release August 20 (covering week ending August 20); FRED API blocked by network egress proxy; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.73T (July 15 estimate) → $6.74T (August 13 H.4.1) = ~+$10B, within the 0.5% flat threshold; status supportive (balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no aggressive QT; July 29 FOMC held at 3.50–3.75%; August 14 soft retail sales reduce September hike probability, lessening near-term QT acceleration risk).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass blocked by network egress proxy — carried forward at +0.004%/8h; BTC dominance at 56.06% on August 15 (down from 56.58% on August 14); total crypto market cap ~$2.29T as market digested soft August 14 retail sales; near-zero positive funding well below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold; 30-day trend down (from ~+0.006%/8h in late June toward near-zero); status supportive (near-zero funding signals healthy positioning without leverage crowding; BTC dominance at 56.06% remains well above the 55% Alt Rotation trigger).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$301B (USDT ~$183.4B, USDC ~$72B) as of August 2026; total crypto market cap ~$2.29T; stablecoin dominance 13.44% (CoinLaw/Statista, August 2026); BTC dominance 56.06%; 30-day trend down: ~14.3% (mid-July) → 13.44% (August 15) = -0.86pp compression as capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets over 30 days; status supportive (30-day declining trend intact; headwind condition requires dominance rising WHILE TOTAL market is also rising — TOTAL declined recently, so headwind condition not met).

upcoming.title: Empire State Manufacturing Index (August 2026)
upcoming.note: NY Federal Reserve Empire State Manufacturing Survey for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — first August regional manufacturing read; cross-checks whether the July ISM surge to 55.6% (4-year high) extended into August despite hot core CPI (3.1%, August 12), July NFP shock (−23,000), and soft July retail sales (August 14, below +0.3% MoM consensus); DXY at 99.63 and 2s10s steepening to +51bps after retail sales suggest markets are pricing in a slower September; a positive Empire State reading (>0) would confirm manufacturing resilience and support BTC Accumulation heading into FOMC Minutes (August 19) and the Jackson Hole–PCE cluster (August 26–28).

upcoming.title: Housing Starts & Building Permits (July 2026)
upcoming.note: US Census Bureau Housing Starts and Building Permits for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — housing remains sensitive to real yields (~2.38%, above the 2% headwind threshold); August 14 soft retail sales pushed DXY to 99.63 and 2Y yields sharply lower, partially easing mortgage rate pressure at the margin; released one day before FOMC Minutes (August 19); any improvement in July housing data despite elevated real yields would signal sector resilience and add a positive data point ahead of PCE (August 26) and Jackson Hole (August 27–29).

upcoming.title: FOMC Minutes (July 28–29, 2026 Meeting)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases minutes of the July 28–29, 2026 FOMC meeting at 2:00 PM ET — three weeks after the July 29 policy decision (held at 3.50–3.75%, 9-3 vote, most divided since 2016); by release markets will have processed July NFP (−23,000, Aug 7), hot core CPI (3.1% YoY, Aug 12), benign July PPI (Aug 13), and soft July retail sales (Aug 14; DXY fell to 99.63, 2s10s steepened to +51bps); key signals: (1) degree of consensus for September hike vs. cut — soft retail sales reinforce the case against a September hike; (2) how the three dissenters characterized the inflation/labor trade-off; (3) any explicit forward guidance thresholds; Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote (August 28) is the next major catalyst after the minutes.

upcoming.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Survey (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Philadelphia Federal Reserve Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — second August regional manufacturing read; cross-checks Empire State (August 17) and the July ISM surge (55.6%) against hot core CPI (3.1%) cost pressure, July NFP shock (−23,000), and soft July retail sales (August 14); released the day after FOMC Minutes (August 19); a positive print alongside Empire State would reinforce manufacturing resilience and sustain BTC Accumulation heading into PCE (August 26) and Jackson Hole.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 15, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 15, 2026 — fourth consecutive weekly labor read post-July NFP shock (−23,000, August 7); prior weeks showed claims below 215K; released alongside Philly Fed on August 20, one day after FOMC Minutes; a sustained rise in claims above 215K+ alongside negative NFP and soft retail sales would deepen the stagflationary picture heading into PCE (August 26) and Jackson Hole (August 27–29).

upcoming.title: S&P Global Flash PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: S&P Global Flash PMI preliminary estimates for August 2026 at 9:45 AM ET — first composite activity read for August; July 2026: Manufacturing 53.8, Services 53.6; the August read is the first broad activity gauge post-NFP shock (−23,000), hot core CPI (3.1%, August 12), FOMC Minutes (August 19), and soft July retail sales (August 14); DXY falling to 99.63 on soft data signals markets are repricing September; a soft August flash PMI alongside weak retail sales would validate recession-risk concerns and complicate the hot-CPI picture; a stable read supports BTC Accumulation heading into PCE (August 26) and Jackson Hole (August 27–29).
